title: Pseudo-observations from a return panel
deliverables: per-date table [T x N]: u per asset
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices or returns [T x N] with dates. DITANYAKAN: pseudo-observations U [T x N] in (0,1). RUMUS: card Core 1 u_ij = rank_ij/(T+1), average ranks for ties (card V1 a; alternatives R/T, (R-0.5)/T only if stated); toolkit pseudo_observations(x). JAWAB: 1) sort dates; log returns from close if prices. 2) drop NaN rows jointly -> common [T]. 3) rank each column (rankdata 'average'). 4) divide by T+1. 5) check 0 < u < 1, column means 0.5.
pitfalls: ranks/T gives u = 1 and infinite quantiles

title: Kendall tau matrix (tau-b) across assets
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N]. DITANYAKAN: tau matrix [N x N] (unit diagonal, symmetric) and/or per-pair list. RUMUS: card Core 2 tau-b via scipy.stats.kendalltau or pandas corr('kendall') (card V3 a); same on raw data and pseudo-obs; toolkit empirical_kendall_tau(u). JAWAB: 1) clean returns jointly. 2) for each pair in the stated asset order (itertools.combinations), key 'A-B'. 3) tau. 4) fill symmetric matrix. 5) check |tau| <= 1.
pitfalls: alphabetical pair order instead of stated order

title: Kendall tau-a by counting concordant and discordant pairs
deliverables: summary json: concordant, discordant, ties, tau_a, tau_b
frame: DIKETAHUI: paired samples x, y [n]. DITANYAKAN: C, D, tau-a (and tau-b for comparison). RUMUS: card Core 2 for i<j sign((x_i - x_j)(y_i - y_j)): +1 concordant, -1 discordant, 0 tie; tau_a = (C - D)/C(n,2); tau_b adjusts for ties (card V3 b when 'tau-a' is named). JAWAB: 1) vectorised sign outer products (upper triangle). 2) C, D, ties. 3) tau_a. 4) scipy tau_b. 5) note equality without ties.
pitfalls: O(n^2) memory for large n: loop in chunks

title: Spearman rho matrix and relation to Pearson on ranks
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N]. DITANYAKAN: Spearman matrix. RUMUS: card Core 2 rho_S = Pearson correlation of ranks (or pseudo-obs) = 1 - 6 sum d^2/(n(n^2-1)) without ties; scipy spearmanr / pandas corr('spearman'); toolkit empirical_spearman_rho(u). JAWAB: 1) clean jointly. 2) ranks. 3) Pearson on ranks. 4) matrix. 5) check equal to 12 mean(u v) - 3 approx on pseudo-obs.

title: Gaussian copula by Kendall tau inversion with PSD repair
deliverables: matrix [N x N]: copula correlation R
summary json: min eigenvalue before, after
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N]. DITANYAKAN: Gaussian copula R by tau inversion. RUMUS: card Core 3 R_ij = sin(pi tau_ij/2); card Completing: if min eigenvalue < 0, clip eigenvalues to eps, rebuild V diag(lam) V', rescale to unit diagonal (or Higham nearest correlation); toolkit copula_param_from_tau('gaussian', tau). JAWAB: 1) tau matrix. 2) elementwise sine. 3) eigen-check. 4) repair if needed. 5) check symmetric, unit diagonal, PSD.
formulas: R* = D^-1/2 V max(L, eps) V' D^-1/2
pitfalls: inverting Pearson instead of tau

title: Gaussian copula by Spearman rho inversion
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N] or Spearman matrix. DITANYAKAN: Gaussian copula R from Spearman. RUMUS: card Core 3 Gaussian only: rho = 2 sin(pi rho_S/6); toolkit copula_param_from_spearman('gaussian', rho_s). Not valid for t copula (no closed form; numerical). JAWAB: 1) Spearman matrix. 2) transform elementwise. 3) PSD repair if needed. 4) compare with tau-based R.
pitfalls: using sin(pi tau/2) on Spearman

title: Gaussian copula canonical maximum likelihood (bivariate)
deliverables: summary json: rho, loglik, aic, bic
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]. DITANYAKAN: rho_hat, LL, AIC, BIC. RUMUS: card Core 5 Gaussian log density with x = Phi^-1(u), y = Phi^-1(v); maximise over rho in (-1,1) (bounded scalar); card Core 6 k = 1; toolkit fit_copula('gaussian', u, method='mle'). JAWAB: 1) pseudo-obs. 2) normal scores. 3) bounded minimise of -LL. 4) AIC = -2LL + 2, BIC = -2LL + ln n. 5) check rho close to sin(pi tau/2).

title: Multivariate Gaussian copula MLE closed form
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x N]. DITANYAKAN: R and LL. RUMUS: Z = Phi^-1(U); approximate MLE R = corr(Z) (exact MLE: Z'Z/T rescaled to unit diagonal); LL = -T/2 ln|R| - 0.5 sum_t z_t'(R^-1 - I) z_t; k = N(N-1)/2. JAWAB: 1) normal scores. 2) R. 3) LL via slogdet and solve. 4) AIC/BIC with k. 5) check LL >= 0 relative to independence.
pitfalls: ln det via det overflow (use slogdet)

title: Student-t copula: rho by tau, nu by profile likelihood
deliverables: summary json: rho, nu, loglik, aic, bic
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]; nu bounds (2, 50]. DITANYAKAN: rho, nu, LL, AIC, BIC (k=2). RUMUS: card V4 a: rho = sin(pi tau/2); card Core 5 t log density with x = t_nu^-1(u); maximise LL over nu by bounded 1-D search; toolkit fit_copula('t', u, method='itau' or as available, nu_bounds). JAWAB: 1) tau -> rho. 2) LL(nu) with rho fixed. 3) minimize_scalar bounded. 4) AIC, BIC. 5) check LL >= Gaussian LL (approx), nu at bound reported.
formulas: ln c = ln f2(x,y) - ln f1(x) - ln f1(y)
pitfalls: using Phi^-1 instead of t_nu^-1 scores

title: Student-t copula joint ML of rho and nu
deliverables: summary json: rho, nu, loglik, aic, bic
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]. DITANYAKAN: (rho, nu) jointly (card V4 b). RUMUS: card Core 5 t density; maximise over rho in (-1,1), nu in (2, nu_max] (L-BFGS-B or transform rho = tanh(a), nu = 2 + exp(b)); start from tau-inversion rho and profile nu. JAWAB: 1) start values. 2) optimise. 3) LL, AIC = -2LL + 4, BIC = -2LL + 2 ln n. 4) compare to profile result.
pitfalls: ln(gammaln) instead of gammaln

title: Clayton copula by tau inversion
deliverables: summary json: tau, theta, lambda_l, lambda_u
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs or returns [T x 2]. DITANYAKAN: theta, tail dependence. RUMUS: card Core 4 theta = 2tau/(1-tau); lambda_L = 2^(-1/theta), lambda_U = 0; tau <= 0 -> independence theta = 0 (card Conventions); toolkit copula_param_from_tau('clayton', tau), tail_dependence('clayton', theta). JAWAB: 1) tau. 2) theta. 3) tail coefficients. 4) optional LL at theta.
pitfalls: negative theta returned as NaN for tau <= 0

title: Clayton copula canonical ML
deliverables: summary json: theta, loglik, aic, bic
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]. DITANYAKAN: theta_hat, LL, AIC, BIC. RUMUS: card Core 5 ln c = ln(1+theta) - (1+theta)(ln u + ln v) - (2 + 1/theta) ln(u^-theta + v^-theta - 1); bounded search theta in (eps, theta_max); compute u^-theta as exp(-theta ln u) to avoid overflow; toolkit fit_copula('clayton', u). JAWAB: 1) pseudo-obs, clip [1e-12, 1-1e-12]. 2) maximise. 3) criteria k = 1. 4) check theta near 2tau/(1-tau).
formulas: ln c = ln(1+theta) - (1+theta)(ln u + ln v) - (2+1/theta) ln(u^-theta + v^-theta - 1)
pitfalls: overflow for large theta

title: Gumbel copula by tau inversion and ML
deliverables: summary json: theta_itau, theta_mle, loglik, lambda_u
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]. DITANYAKAN: theta (inversion and ML), LL, lambda_U. RUMUS: card Core 4 theta = 1/(1-tau), theta >= 1, tau <= 0 -> theta = 1 (LL = 0); lambda_U = 2 - 2^(1/theta); card Core 5 Gumbel log density with a = -ln u, b = -ln v, S = a^theta + b^theta. JAWAB: 1) tau -> theta0. 2) bounded ML on [1, theta_max]. 3) LL, AIC, BIC. 4) lambda_U.
pitfalls: allowing theta < 1

title: Frank copula by tau inversion with the Debye function
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]. DITANYAKAN: Frank theta by tau inversion (and ML). RUMUS: card Core 4 tau = 1 - (4/theta)(1 - D1(theta)), D1(x) = (1/x) int_0^x t/(e^t - 1) dt (quad); solve with brentq on a bracket of sign theta; theta -> 0 independence; negative tau allowed; toolkit copula_tau('frank', theta), copula_param_from_tau('frank', tau). JAWAB: 1) tau. 2) bracket. 3) brentq. 4) LL from card Core 5 Frank density. 5) lambda_L = lambda_U = 0.
pitfalls: bracket including 0 (removable singularity)

title: Copula family selection per pair by AIC and BIC
deliverables: per pair x family table: pair, family, params, loglik, aic, bic, lambda_l, lambda_u
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N]; families list. DITANYAKAN: one row per pair x family; best by AIC (or BIC). RUMUS: card Core 1 -> 5 -> 6 -> 4; k = 1 except t (k = 2); toolkit select_copula(u, families, criterion), fit_copula, tail_dependence. JAWAB: 1) clean jointly. 2) pseudo-obs. 3) for pair in combinations (stated order): fit each family. 4) LL, AIC, BIC, tail coefficients. 5) argmin per pair. 6) check rows = C(N,2) x families, BIC - AIC = k(ln n - 2).
pitfalls: using T-1 vs T inconsistently for n in BIC

title: Parametric tail dependence coefficients per family
deliverables: per-family table: family, theta, nu, lambda_l, lambda_u
frame: DIKETAHUI: fitted families with parameters. DITANYAKAN: lambda_L, lambda_U per family. RUMUS: card Core 4: Clayton lambda_L = 2^(-1/theta), lambda_U = 0; Gumbel lambda_U = 2 - 2^(1/theta), lambda_L = 0; t: lambda = 2 t_{nu+1}(-sqrt((nu+1)(1-rho)/(1+rho))) both tails; Gaussian, Frank 0; toolkit tail_dependence(family, theta, nu). JAWAB: 1) parameters. 2) formulas. 3) table. 4) check 0 <= lambda <= 1.
pitfalls: t cdf with nu instead of nu+1 dof

title: Empirical tail dependence at a quantile threshold
deliverables: summary json: q, lambda_u_hat, lambda_l_hat, counts
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]; q. DITANYAKAN: lambda_U(q), lambda_L(q). RUMUS: card Core 7 lambda_U(q) = #(u>q & v>q)/#(u>q); lambda_L(q) = #(u<1-q & v<1-q)/#(u<1-q); strict inequalities, condition on FIRST variable; alternative denominator n(1-q) when stated; toolkit empirical_tail_dependence(u, q, tail, denominator). JAWAB: 1) pseudo-obs. 2) counts. 3) ratios. 4) check in [0,1].
pitfalls: lower-tail threshold q instead of 1-q

title: Empirical tail dependence curve over thresholds
deliverables: per-q table: q, lambda_u, lambda_l, n_tail
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]; q grid [G]. DITANYAKAN: lambda_U(q), lambda_L(q) per q; optional fitted-model values. RUMUS: card Core 7 per q; model counterpart (1 - 2q + C(q,q))/(1-q) upper and C(1-q,1-q)/(1-q) lower (toolkit copula_cdf). JAWAB: 1) loop q. 2) empirical values and counts. 3) model values for fitted families. 4) table; note Gaussian finite-q values positive though limit 0.
pitfalls: over-interpreting tiny tail counts

title: Sampling a d-dimensional Gaussian copula
deliverables: summary json: empirical tau vs target
frame: DIKETAHUI: R [d x d]; n; seed; RNG API. DITANYAKAN: U [n x d]. RUMUS: card Core 8 L = chol(R); eps ~ N(0, I) [n x d]; Z = eps L'; U = Phi(Z); toolkit copula_sample('gaussian', R, n, d, seed). JAWAB: 1) rng = default_rng(seed) (V5). 2) Cholesky (repair R if not PD). 3) draw, transform. 4) check margins uniform, tau ~ (2/pi) arcsin(rho).
formulas: Z = eps L', L L' = R
pitfalls: Z = eps L (wrong orientation for row samples)

title: Sampling a Student-t copula with shared chi-square
frame: DIKETAHUI: R, nu, n, seed. DITANYAKAN: U [n x d]. RUMUS: card Core 8 Z = eps L'; W ~ chi2(nu) ONE per row; T = Z/sqrt(W/nu); U = t_nu.cdf(T); toolkit copula_sample('t', R, n, nu=nu, seed). JAWAB: 1) rng once. 2) Z [n x d]. 3) W [n, 1]. 4) T, U. 5) check tau target and joint tail counts > Gaussian.
formulas: T = Z / sqrt(W/nu), W ~ chi2(nu) per row
pitfalls: independent chi2 per coordinate

title: Sampling Clayton by conditional inversion
frame: DIKETAHUI: theta; n; seed. DITANYAKAN: (U1, U2) [n x 2]. RUMUS: card Core 8 U1, W iid U(0,1); U2 = (U1^-theta (W^(-theta/(1+theta)) - 1) + 1)^(-1/theta). JAWAB: 1) rng once; draw U1 then W (stated order). 2) U2. 3) check tau ~ theta/(theta+2), lower-tail clustering.
pitfalls: drawing [n x 2] in one call vs two calls changes the stream

title: Sampling a multivariate Clayton by gamma frailty
frame: DIKETAHUI: theta > 0; d; n; seed. DITANYAKAN: U [n x d]. RUMUS: card Core 8 V ~ Gamma(1/theta, 1) per row; E_i ~ Exp(1) [n x d]; U_i = (1 + E_i/V)^(-1/theta) (generator inverse psi(t) = (1+t)^(-1/theta)). JAWAB: 1) V [n,1]. 2) E [n x d]. 3) U. 4) check pairwise tau all ~ theta/(theta+2).

title: Sampling Gumbel by positive stable frailty
frame: DIKETAHUI: theta >= 1; d; n; seed. DITANYAKAN: U [n x d]. RUMUS: card Core 8 S positive stable index alpha = 1/theta with Laplace transform exp(-t^alpha) (CMS: Theta ~ U(0,pi), W ~ Exp(1), S = sin(alpha Theta)/sin(Theta)^(1/alpha) (sin((1-alpha)Theta)/W)^((1-alpha)/alpha)); U_i = exp(-(E_i/S)^(1/theta)). JAWAB: 1) S [n,1]. 2) E [n x d]. 3) U. 4) check tau ~ 1 - 1/theta, margins uniform.
pitfalls: scipy levy_stable scale/parameterisation makes margins non-uniform

title: Sampling Frank by conditional inversion
frame: DIKETAHUI: theta (any sign, != 0); n; seed. DITANYAKAN: U [n x 2]. RUMUS: card Core 8 U2 = -(1/theta) ln(1 + W(e^-theta - 1)/(W + (1-W) e^(-theta U1))). JAWAB: 1) U1, W. 2) U2. 3) check tau target, symmetry, no tail clustering.

title: Copula simulation with parametric margins to portfolio VaR
deliverables: summary json: var, es per level
frame: DIKETAHUI: copula and parameters; margins F_i (normal/t with params); weights [d]; value V; n; seed; level. DITANYAKAN: VaR, ES of portfolio. RUMUS: card Completing: U from copula (Core 8), X_i = F_i^-1(U_i); r_p = X w; L = -V r_p; VaR = quantile, ES = tail mean (stated quantile rule). JAWAB: 1) sample U. 2) marginal ppf. 3) portfolio losses. 4) VaR, ES. 5) compare across copulas with same margins.
pitfalls: comparing copulas with different seeds per family when 'set once'

title: Copula with empirical margins (historical marginal quantiles)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x d]; fitted copula; n; seed; weights. DITANYAKAN: simulated returns and portfolio VaR/ES. RUMUS: X_i = empirical quantile of column i at U_i (np.quantile with stated method, or sorted[ceil(U T)-1]); then portfolio as usual. JAWAB: 1) fit copula on pseudo-obs. 2) simulate U. 3) marginal empirical quantiles. 4) portfolio VaR/ES. 5) note margins cannot exceed historical extremes.

title: Pearson correlation of simulated returns vs copula rho
frame: DIKETAHUI: copula (rho or theta); margins; n; seed. DITANYAKAN: Pearson of X, Kendall of X, compare with copula parameter. RUMUS: card Completing: Pearson of X must be computed (depends on margins); tau invariant under increasing transforms -> tau(X) = tau(U) = copula tau. JAWAB: 1) simulate U, X. 2) Pearson(X), Kendall(X). 3) report differences; check Kendall matches formula.
pitfalls: treating Pearson as copula parameter

title: Copula CDF and joint lower-orthant probability
frame: DIKETAHUI: family, parameter; points (u, v) [M] or marginal levels x, y with margins. DITANYAKAN: P(U<=u, V<=v) = C(u,v). RUMUS: Gaussian Phi2(Phi^-1(u), Phi^-1(v); rho) (toolkit bivariate_normal_cdf); Clayton (u^-theta + v^-theta - 1)^(-1/theta); Gumbel exp(-((-ln u)^theta + (-ln v)^theta)^(1/theta)); Frank -(1/theta) ln(1 + (e^-theta u - 1)(e^-theta v - 1)/(e^-theta - 1)); toolkit copula_cdf. JAWAB: 1) u = F_X(x). 2) C. 3) check Frechet bounds max(u+v-1,0) <= C <= min(u,v).

title: Joint exceedance probability via the survival copula
frame: DIKETAHUI: copula; margins; thresholds (x, y). DITANYAKAN: P(X > x, Y > y); for losses P(L1 > l1, L2 > l2). RUMUS: P = 1 - u - v + C(u, v), u = F_X(x), v = F_Y(y); for return downside P(X <= x, Y <= y) = C(u,v). JAWAB: 1) marginal probabilities. 2) C. 3) survival formula. 4) compare with independence product (1-u)(1-v).
pitfalls: using C directly for an upper-tail event

title: Conditional probability of a joint crash
frame: DIKETAHUI: copula; quantile level p for both assets. DITANYAKAN: P(V <= p | U <= p) and upper analogue. RUMUS: P(V<=p | U<=p) = C(p,p)/p; P(V>q | U>q) = (1 - 2q + C(q,q))/(1-q); limit gives lambda. JAWAB: 1) C(p,p). 2) ratio. 3) compare families at equal tau. 4) report.

title: Conditional copula h-function given an exact value
frame: DIKETAHUI: family, parameter; (u, v) points. DITANYAKAN: h(v|u) = P(V <= v | U = u). RUMUS: Gaussian Phi((Phi^-1(v) - rho Phi^-1(u))/sqrt(1-rho^2)); t: t_{nu+1}((y - rho x)/sqrt((nu + x^2)(1-rho^2)/(nu+1))); Clayton u^(-theta-1)(u^-theta + v^-theta - 1)^(-1-1/theta); numerical dC/du otherwise. JAWAB: 1) formula per family. 2) evaluate. 3) check in [0,1], increasing in v.
formulas: t h: t_{nu+1}((y - rho x) sqrt((nu+1)/((nu+x^2)(1-rho^2))))

title: Joint default probability of two names under a Gaussian copula
deliverables: summary json: p1, p2, joint_pd, default_correlation
frame: DIKETAHUI: marginal PDs p1, p2 over horizon; copula (asset) correlation rho. DITANYAKAN: P(both default), default correlation. RUMUS: p12 = Phi2(Phi^-1(p1), Phi^-1(p2); rho) (toolkit bivariate_normal_cdf); rho_D = (p12 - p1 p2)/sqrt(p1(1-p1)p2(1-p2)). JAWAB: 1) thresholds. 2) bivariate cdf. 3) default correlation. 4) check rho_D << rho for small PDs.
pitfalls: confusing asset correlation with default correlation

title: Li Gaussian copula default times simulation
frame: DIKETAHUI: hazards lambda_i [d]; correlation R; horizon T; n; seed. DITANYAKAN: default times [n x d]; P(first default <= T). RUMUS: Li (2000): U from Gaussian copula (card Core 8); tau_i = -ln(1 - U_i)/lambda_i (or -ln U_i, same law); first default = min_i tau_i; P(FtD <= T) = mean(min tau <= T). JAWAB: 1) sample U. 2) invert exponential survival. 3) min per row. 4) probabilities. 5) check marginal PD ~ 1 - e^(-lambda T).

title: nth-to-default basket probability by copula Monte Carlo
frame: DIKETAHUI: PDs or hazards [d]; copula (Gaussian or t) with R (nu); T; n; seed. DITANYAKAN: distribution of default count by T; P(at least k). RUMUS: default_i = 1{U_i <= p_i} with p_i = 1 - e^(-lambda_i T); N_def = sum_i; P(N >= k) = mean. JAWAB: 1) sample U. 2) indicators. 3) count histogram [d+1]. 4) tail probabilities. 5) compare Gaussian vs t (t fattens extreme counts).

title: One-factor Gaussian copula conditional default probability
frame: DIKETAHUI: PD p; correlation rho; factor grid or level q. DITANYAKAN: p(M) and portfolio loss fraction quantile. RUMUS: A_i = sqrt(rho) M + sqrt(1-rho) e_i; p(M) = Phi((Phi^-1(p) - sqrt(rho) M)/sqrt(1-rho)); LHP quantile at q: Phi((Phi^-1(p) + sqrt(rho) Phi^-1(q))/sqrt(1-rho)) (toolkit vasicek_loss_quantile); MC one_factor_mc_losses. JAWAB: 1) p(M). 2) quantile or integrate over M. 3) LGD scaling if given.

title: Archimedean copula from its generator
deliverables: summary json: generator, tau, C at points
frame: DIKETAHUI: generator phi (or its inverse psi); parameter. DITANYAKAN: C(u,v), Kendall tau. RUMUS: C(u,v) = phi^-1(phi(u) + phi(v)); tau = 1 + 4 int_0^1 phi(t)/phi'(t) dt; Clayton phi = (t^-theta - 1)/theta; Gumbel phi = (-ln t)^theta; Frank phi = -ln((e^(-theta t) - 1)/(e^-theta - 1)). JAWAB: 1) phi, phi^-1. 2) evaluate C. 3) tau by quad. 4) check against closed forms (Core 4).

title: Rotated and survival copulas
deliverables: per-family table: family, rotation, theta, loglik, lambda_l, lambda_u
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]; base families; rotations. DITANYAKAN: fit rotated families; tail coefficients. RUMUS: survival (180): c180(u,v) = c(1-u, 1-v), tails swap (survival Clayton has lambda_U = 2^(-1/theta)); 90: c(1-u, v), 270: c(u, 1-v) for negative dependence. JAWAB: 1) transform data. 2) fit base family on transformed. 3) LL unchanged formula. 4) report swapped tails. 5) include in AIC selection.
pitfalls: forgetting to swap the tail coefficients

title: Evaluating copula log-likelihood at given parameters
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]; family and parameter(s). DITANYAKAN: LL = sum ln c(u_t, v_t). RUMUS: card Core 5 per family; toolkit copula_logpdf(family, u, theta, nu), copula_loglik. Independence LL = 0; t LL -> Gaussian as nu -> inf. JAWAB: 1) clip u. 2) log densities. 3) sum. 4) sanity checks.
formulas: LL = sum_t ln c(u_t, v_t; theta)
pitfalls: exp-then-log underflow (stay in logs)

title: IFM: parametric margins then copula ML
deliverables: summary json: copula params, loglik_copula, loglik_total
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [T x N]; margin family per asset; copula family. DITANYAKAN: margin parameters, copula parameters, LL (copula and total). RUMUS: card V2 c: stage 1 MLE each margin (norm.fit, t.fit); u_it = F_i(x_it; theta_i); stage 2 maximise copula LL on u; total LL = sum_i sum_t ln f_i + sum_t ln c. JAWAB: 1) fit margins. 2) PIT to u. 3) copula fit. 4) LL components. 5) compare with CML.
formulas: LL_total = sum ln f_i + sum ln c

title: Empirical copula and Cramer-von Mises goodness of fit
frame: DIKETAHUI: pseudo-obs [T x 2]; fitted family; B; seed. DITANYAKAN: S_n and bootstrap p-value. RUMUS: C_n(u,v) = (1/T) sum 1{U_t <= u, V_t <= v}; S_n = sum_t (C_n(u_t,v_t) - C_theta(u_t,v_t))^2 (Genest-Remillard-Beaudoin 2009); bootstrap: simulate from C_theta, re-rank, refit, recompute S_n; p = mean(S_n* >= S_n). JAWAB: 1) C_n at data. 2) S_n. 3) B loops. 4) p-value.
pitfalls: not re-ranking bootstrap samples

title: Spearman rho implied by a parametric copula
deliverables: per-family table: family, theta, tau, rho_s
frame: DIKETAHUI: families with parameters (often matched to one tau). DITANYAKAN: rho_S per family. RUMUS: Gaussian rho_S = (6/pi) arcsin(rho/2); general rho_S = 12 int int C(u,v) du dv - 3 (dblquad) or MC; Frank closed form via Debye D2; toolkit spearman_rho(family, theta, nu). JAWAB: 1) parameters. 2) rho_S. 3) table showing rho_S differs across families at equal tau (card Invariants).
formulas: rho_S = 12 int int C du dv - 3

title: Frechet-Hoeffding bounds, comonotonic and countermonotonic
deliverables: per-point table: u, v, W, Pi, M, C
frame: DIKETAHUI: copula C; points [M]. DITANYAKAN: bounds and check W <= C <= M. RUMUS: W = max(u+v-1, 0), Pi = u v, M = min(u, v); comonotonic: V = U (tau = 1); countermonotonic: V = 1 - U (tau = -1). JAWAB: 1) evaluate. 2) check inequality. 3) worst-case VaR of a sum uses comonotone for VaR additivity.

title: Attainable Pearson correlation bounds for lognormal margins
frame: DIKETAHUI: lognormal sigma1, sigma2. DITANYAKAN: attainable Pearson range. RUMUS: rho_max = (e^(sigma1 sigma2) - 1)/sqrt((e^(sigma1^2) - 1)(e^(sigma2^2) - 1)); rho_min with -sigma1 sigma2 (Embrechts-McNeil-Straumann 2002).
